title: Expected-answer record for one validated checkout
description: What one checkout's run is judged against, stored at specs/023-extension-repo-profile/expected/<slug>.json. Written by reading the checkout's code and committed before the first run against it, never derived from the run it judges. Exhaustive over the checkout's analysis scope: a declared type the run produces and the record lacks is a mismatch, so an omission cannot be scored as accuracy. Every identifier is the full name the graph uses, which is the string a mismatch prints.

schemaVersion.description: Format version. A record without this, or with any other value, is not read.

repository.description: The checkout's name. It identifies the checkout without a path, so the record stays portable and carries no machine-specific path.

source.description: One sentence saying how and when the record was read out of the checkout's code. Prose for a reviewer; the comparison never reads it.

types.description: Every declared type inside the checkout's analysis scope. An empty array claims the checkout declares none, and that claim is checked.

links.description: Every view-to-view-model pair the checkout states. A pair the run finds and the record lacks is an invented link; a pair the record names and the run does not find is a missing link.

findings.description: Every finding known to be true of the checkout, and no others: a finding the run produces and the record lacks is a finding the run invented, which is what a convention mismatch looks like.

typeName.description: A full name with at least one namespace segment, matching the node id the graph emits.

file.description: Checkout-relative path with forward slashes, so a reviewer can open the declaration. A view is usually declared in its .cs code-behind; one with no code-behind is named by its .xaml. No leading slash and no drive letter.

layer.description: The layer the checkout's own conventions give this type, read from its code rather than from the extension's output.

types.description: The full names the finding is about, sorted, so a match does not depend on the wording of a title.
